learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels Explained
learn.intro: Bifacial solar panels capture sunlight from both sides, boosting efficiency by up to 30% compared to traditional panels. This innovation accelerates solar adoption by maximizing energy yield in limited space, crucial for India's renewable energy goals.
learn.c1_text: Bifacial panels absorb direct sunlight on the front and reflected light from the ground on the back. Albedo surfaces like white roofs or sand enhance this effect. A 100 kW bifacial system in Rajasthan could produce 20% more energy annually than monofacial panels.
learn.c2_text: These panels achieve 20-25% efficiency by utilizing scattered and reflected light. Elevated mounting allows ground reflection capture. In India, bifacial panels are ideal for utility-scale projects in high-albedo regions like Gujarat's solar parks.
learn.c3_text: India's National Solar Mission incentivizes bifacial technology. Projects like the 1 GW Bhadla Solar Park use these panels to maximize output in Rajasthan's high-solar-irradiance zone. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy supports their integration in large-scale solar initiatives.
learn.stat2: Bifacial panels increase energy yield by 15-30%
learn.stat3: Albedo of white surfaces: 0.8 vs ground: 0.2-0.5

learn.title: Second Life EV Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: Second-life EV batteries repurpose used electric vehicle batteries for grid storage, extending their lifecycle and reducing waste. This approach supports India's renewable integration by providing cost-effective energy storage solutions for balancing supply and demand.
learn.c1_text: After automotive use, batteries retain 70-80% capacity for stationary storage. Testing and refurbishing ensures safety. For example, a retired Tata Motors EV battery can store 40 kWh for 10 years, powering 4 Indian households daily.
learn.c2_text: Second-life batteries cost 30-50% less than new units. They reduce lithium mining demand by 20% per kWh stored. India's EV boom (1.5 million sold in 2023) creates a growing secondary market for grid storage projects.
learn.c3_text: Indian startups like SunFuel Energy partner with Tata Motors to deploy second-life batteries in rural microgrids. The government's FAME II scheme promotes EV adoption, while NITI Aayog's Hydrogen Roadmap includes battery recycling infrastructure.
learn.stat1: India EV sales reached 1.5 million units (2023)
learn.stat2: Second-life batteries cost 40% less than new ones
learn.stat3: 90% of EV batteries can be repurposed after automotive use

learn.title: Levelised Cost of Energy (LCOE) Explained
learn.intro: LCOE measures the lifetime cost per kWh of power generation, enabling fair comparisons between technologies. Tracking LCOE trends is vital for India's energy transition, guiding investments in solar, wind, and traditional sources toward optimal solutions.
learn.c1_text: LCOE = (Total lifetime costs) / (Total energy output). It includes capital, O&M, and fuel costs. For example, India's solar LCOE dropped to $0.026/kWh in 2023, outcompeting coal's $0.08/kWh, making renewables economically dominant.
learn.c2_text: Policymakers use LCOE to prioritize low-cost projects. India's renewable energy auctions mandate LCOE-based tariff bidding, ensuring affordable power. The 2023 IRENA report shows solar LCOE fell 89% since 2010, driving global adoption.
learn.c3_text: India's National Energy Policy targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, guided by LCOE analysis. States like Gujarat leverage low solar LCOE ($0.024/kWh) to replace diesel generators, while wind projects in Tamil Nadu benefit from favorable LCOE comparisons with thermal plants.
learn.stat4: India aims for 500 GW non-fossil by 2030

learn.title: Solar PV Panels & the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar PV panels convert sunlight into electricity using the photoelectric effect, where photons knock electrons loose from semiconductor materials. This fundamental process powers India's 90 GW solar capacity, making it a cornerstone of the clean energy transition.
learn.c1_text: When photons strike silicon wafers in PV cells, they energize electrons, creating electric current. A 1 m² panel generates 150-200 W under 1,000 W/m² sunlight. This principle, discovered by Einstein in 1905, underpins all solar technology.
learn.c2_text: PV cells use doped silicon layers: n-type (electrons) and p-type (holes). A p-n junction creates an electric field. Monocrystalline cells achieve 22% efficiency, while India's arid climate optimizes solar irradiance (5-6 kWh/m²/day), boosting output.
learn.c3_text: India's 90 GW solar capacity (2024) includes 25 GW from rooftop systems. The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission targets 100 GW by 2022, leveraging PV technology. States like Rajasthan and Gujarat lead with utility-scale projects, benefiting from high solar insolation.
learn.stat4: 1 m² panel produces 150-200 W under standard conditions

learn.title: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Technology Explained
learn.intro: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology allows electric vehicles to discharge power back to the grid, enhancing stability and renewable integration. This bidirectional charging supports India's grid modernization by leveraging EV batteries as distributed energy resources during peak demand periods.
learn.c1_text: V2G enables EVs to both charge from and supply the grid. A 60 kWh Nissan Leaf can provide 150 kWh/day to the grid. In India, this reduces grid instability by 10-15% during peak hours, as demonstrated in pilot projects with Tata Motors' EVs.
learn.c2_text: V2G provides frequency regulation and peak shaving. With 30 million Indian EVs projected by 2030, aggregated V2G capacity could reach 180 GWh, equivalent to a 10 GW gas plant. This reduces curtailment of solar/wind energy by 20-30% in states like Karnataka.
learn.c3_text: The Energy Networking Consortium's Delhi pilot uses Nissan Leaf EVs to stabilize the grid. The Ministry of Power's Ujjwal Bharat scheme promotes V2G in urban areas. Tata Power andissan are testing V2G in Mumbai, aiming to integrate 50,000 EVs by 2025 for grid support services.
learn.stat3: Aggregated V2G capacity: 180 GWh potential by 2030
learn.stat4: Tata Motors EV pilot in Delhi shows 10% grid stability improvement

learn.title: Green Hydrogen via Water Electrolysis
learn.intro: Green hydrogen is produced through water electrolysis using renewable electricity, offering a carbon-free fuel for hard-to-abate sectors. India's National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 MT production by 2030, positioning electrolysis as critical for decarbonizing industry and transport.
learn.c1_text: PEM electrolyzers use platinum catalysts for rapid response to variable renewables, operating at 80-90% efficiency. Alkaline systems use potassium hydroxide, achieving 75-85% efficiency but requiring steady power. PEM costs $1,000/kW vs alkaline's $800/kW, but declining rapidly.
learn.c2_text: PEM excels in dynamic conditions, ideal for solar/wind integration. Alkaline suits large-scale baseload production. India's Adani Green Energy plans a 1 GW PEM plant in Tamil Nadu, while Bharat Petroleum uses alkaline systems for refinery hydrogen needs, reducing emissions by 1.5 million tons CO₂/year.
learn.c3_text: The $23 billion National Green Hydrogen Mission funds 125 projects by 2025. Gujarat's Dahej plant will produce 100,000 tons/year using 2 GW solar power. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy mandates electrolyzer procurement standards, accelerating domestic manufacturing under the PLI scheme.
learn.stat1: India's green hydrogen target: 5 MT by 2030
learn.stat4: Adani's 1 GW PEM plant in Tamil Nadu under construction
